strings.name: Simon Stiell
strings.role: Executive Secretary of the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
strings.summary: Simon Stiell is a Grenadian politician and international climate official with a background in engineering, business management and government. He became UNFCCC Executive Secretary in 2022 and was reappointed in 2025. He leads the secretariat in supporting negotiations, climate-information review and implementation, and advocates for mitigation, adaptation and finance. Conference outcomes are collective decisions of Parties; his influence should be assessed alongside implementation of national commitments and resource gaps.
strings.coverageNote: Information checked through 18 November 2026. UN and university records support the office and education details. The transcript of his delivered COP31 speech on 17 November 2026 supports recent activity and current office. His birth date has not been reliably corroborated and is not carried over from machine-collected material.
strings.influence.rationale: Moved from public affairs in Grenada into leadership of the UN climate institution, promoting international mitigation and climate-finance negotiations.
strings.facts.f1.label: Engineering and management education
strings.facts.f1.value: He trained in engineering at London Metropolitan University and the College of North West London and earned an MBA from the University of Westminster in 1998. Before government service he spent about fourteen years in technology, including roles at Nokia and GEC Plessey Telecommunications. These employers are not presented as companies he founded.
strings.facts.f2.label: From Grenada to Bonn
strings.facts.f2.value: He served in Grenada's government from March 2013 to June 2022, with responsibilities including education, human resources and the environment, and was a senator and Leader of Government Business. In 2022 he became head of the UN climate secretariat in Bonn; he was neither Grenada's prime minister nor the president of successive COP conferences.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Secretariat support and national decisions
strings.highlights.h1.text: The secretariat provides technical analysis, reporting review, negotiation support and the registry of nationally determined contributions. Its executive secretary can coordinate and advocate, while governments formulate and implement their policies and Parties make conference decisions. Global emissions outcomes cannot be wholly credited to one individual.
strings.highlights.h2.title: The gap between finance targets and needs
strings.highlights.h2.text: COP29 set a climate-finance goal of US$300 billion annually by 2035, alongside efforts by all actors to scale broader finance to US$1.3 trillion a year. Delegates from India and other developing countries criticized the deal as inadequate; Stiell also acknowledged that not all expectations were met. Targets, future fundraising and money already disbursed are distinct.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Emphasizing climate transparency at COP31
strings.timeline.t1.text: Speaking at the ministerial transparency dialogue in Antalya, he stressed that government reports should reveal both progress and gaps and inform the second global stocktake. This is a record of a delivered speech, not evidence that the still-ongoing COP31 had already reached its final agreement.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Reappointed for a second three-year term
strings.timeline.t2.text: The UN Secretary-General reappointed him following consultation with the Conference of the Parties through its Bureau. The official biography confirms the month and term length; it does not justify inventing a precise day on which the term ends.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Baku conference adopts a new finance goal
strings.timeline.t3.text: COP29 closed with a new climate-finance goal. Stiell emphasized the need to fulfil promises and acknowledged substantial remaining work. This negotiated outcome belongs to participating countries, rather than representing money he personally raised or spent.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Presenting the Dubai global-stocktake outcome
strings.timeline.t4.text: COP28 completed the first global stocktake, calling for a just, orderly and equitable transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems. In his closing address, Stiell urged implementation of commitments in the real economy. The agreement did not mean the world had already stopped using fossil fuels.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Loss-and-damage fund establishment agreed
strings.timeline.t5.text: COP27 decided to establish new funding arrangements and a dedicated fund to help developing countries address climate-related loss and damage, with a transitional committee to develop implementation recommendations. Establishment, full operation and actual payments are separate stages.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Appointed UN climate executive secretary
strings.timeline.t6.text: The UN Secretary-General announced his appointment, endorsed by the Convention's Bureau. Ibrahim Thiaw was serving in an acting capacity; the previous permanent head was Patricia Espinosa. The appointment marked a move from national politics to international secretariat leadership.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Entering Grenada's government
strings.timeline.t7.text: He began a period of government service lasting until June 2022, covering education, human resources and environmental responsibilities, and led government business in the Senate. Climate Resilience and Environment Minister was one of his portfolios; the whole period should not be assigned a single ministerial title.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completing an MBA
strings.timeline.t8.text: He earned an MBA at the University of Westminster; the university's 2022 account explicitly identifies the graduation year. This management education and his earlier engineering training form part of his professional background in technology and public affairs.
